newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt builds two airports in BOT agreement.
newsitem.headline: Egypt builds two airports in BOT agreement.

text.p: The Egyptian state has built two airports it had previously offered to the private sector and invited businessmen to take over their management, a Civil Aviation Authority official said on Saturday.

Abdel Fattah Kato, chairman of the CAA, told reporters the state had spent about three months and 25 million pounds ($7.4 million) building the airports at the Dakhla and east Oweinat oases in the western desert.
"The authority took the first step and built these airports to attract the private sector to such projects. Private businessmen can still play a role in these airports by managing them," he added.
In January, the state offered private investors the two airports, and three others at the oases of Bahariya and Farafra and the Red Sea resort of Dahab, under a build, operate and transfer agreement.
The airports at Dakhla and east Oweinat can handle only light and medium-weight aircraft. They will be ready to receive flights before the end of next month, Kato added.

The CAA has already offered two other airport projects to build, operate and transfer operators -- Marsa Alam on the Red Sea coast and El Alamein on the Mediterranean. The government is negotiating with the Kuwaiti company Mohamed Abdulmuhsin Kharafi and Sons on the Marsa Alam project, expected to cost about 120 million pounds ($35 million).
